title: Post-incident follow-up: Control plane TLS handshake timeouts during private deployment upgrade
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary:
On 2026-03-09 23:14 UTC we began a staged upgrade of the private control plane agents for several on-prem tenants. During stage 2 (rolling upgrade of control-plane proxies), a subset of customers experienced persistent TLS handshake timeouts between the customer VPCs and the upgraded control-plane endpoints. This caused control-plane RPCs to fail, agent heartbeats to drop, and temporary loss of API operations for affected tenants (control-plane connectivity degraded for ~47 minutes).

Impact:
- Affected tenants: 6 out of 42 private tenants in the staging cohort; 3 were high-SLA customers.
- Customer-visible symptoms: 502/504 errors from control-plane API, delayed agent-heartbeat reconnections, failing config rollouts.
- Duration: ~47 minutes from first observed handshake failures to rollback completion.
- Severity: P0 outage for impacted tenants, overall platform availability not fully degraded due to rollback.

High-level timeline (UTC):
- 23:14:00: Rollout of control-plane proxy v2.9.1 starts (stage 2).
- 23:18:20: First TLS handshake timeout spikes observed in Grafana (proxy->agent metrics).
- 23:19:05: Alerts triggered: control-plane:tls_errors_high and agent-heartbeat-loss.
- 23:21:30: Engineering rotation paged; initial mitigation attempted: increase proxy TLS timeouts.
- 23:28:40: Timeouts persist; rollback to v2.9.0 initiated for stage 2.
- 23:44:10: Rollback complete; handshakes return to normal for most tenants.
- 23:48:30: Post-rollback verification and customer notifications.

Root cause investigation summary:
- Primary cause: A change in proxy TLS client configuration in v2.9.1 (enablement of TLS 1.3-only cipher suite preference and aggressive session ticket reuse) exposed latent incompatibilities in a subset of customer middleboxes and older TLS stacks, causing the server-side handshake to drop or abort.
- Secondary factors: The upgrade orchestration applied simultaneous proxy restarts within single subnets for multiple tenants (due to an orchestration bug in the staged rollout scheduler), increasing blast radius. The combination of incompatible TLS settings and bursty reconnections overwhelmed some upstream NAT timers and middlebox session caches.
- Observability gap: Early metrics for TLS handshake failures were present but lacked per-tenant tagging, which delayed identification of affected customer subset.

Immediate mitigations performed:
- Staged rollback of proxy binaries to v2.9.0 for stage 2 completed by 23:44 UTC.
- Temporarily increased control-plane TLS handshake timeout and backoff to reduce rapid reconnect churn.
- Opened communication to impacted customers with a technical summary and next-steps.

Permanent fixes and action plan (owners and due dates):
1) Revert TLS 1.3-only cipher-suite enforcement in next stable proxy build and publish compatibility notes in release notes. Owner: Marcus Liang. Due: 2026-03-15.
2) Implement TLS compatibility test harness in CI that simulates common middlebox behaviors and older TLS stacks (includes server and client handshake permutations). Owner: Suresh Nair. Due: 2026-04-01.
3) Patch staged rollout scheduler to enforce cross-tenant anti-affinity within the same subnet and limit parallel restarts to 1 per /24. Owner: Lina Romero. Due: 2026-03-22.
4) Add per-tenant tagging for TLS and handshake metrics in Grafana/Prometheus to enable faster root-cause identification. Owner: Observability team (lead: Priya Shah). Due: 2026-03-18.
5) Run a focused compatibility sweep against top 10 customer network appliance signatures prior to next private release; produce a compatibility matrix and customer advisory. Owner: Solutions Engineering (lead: Omar Ruiz). Due: 2026-04-05.
6) Update incident runbook to include immediate fallback: graceful connection drain + 5 minute cooldown before next control-plane restart in same subnet. Owner: SRE (lead: Hannah Kim). Due: 2026-03-16.

Links and artifacts:
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ctl-tls/proxy-handshakes?from=now-2h&to=now
- Incident notes (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INC/2026-03-09+Private+Upgrade+Handshake+Failures
- Rollback PR and logs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/controlplane/pull/4123
- Staged rollout scheduler bug ticket: ENG-9412

Postmortem decisions and acceptance criteria:
- We will not resume the private control-plane rolling upgrades until TLS compatibility tests (action 2) pass for a representative set of customer network behaviors and the rollout scheduler patch (action 3) is deployed to canary.
- Acceptance criteria for GA of proxy v2.9.1 re-release: TLS compatibility test suite green, per-tenant telemetry shows handshake metrics, staged scheduler anti-affinity verified on canary tenants, no regressions in end-to-end upgrade test runs for 48 hours.

Follow-up tickets (creation planned):
- ENG-9753: CI TLS compatibility harness implementation
- ENG-9754: Rollout scheduler anti-affinity patch and e2e test
- ENG-9755: Grafana per-tenant TLS metrics tagging

Notes on stakeholder communications:
- Customer success ran targeted outreach to the 6 impacted tenants and provided mitigation guidance; churn risk assessed as low due to rapid rollback and SLA credits offered.
- Sales and Legal notified for the three high-SLA customers; all opted for immediate postmortem review meeting.

Longer-term platform learnings:
- Feature gates are required for any transport-level configuration changes for private deployments; defaults should remain maximally compatible and opt-in for stricter profiles.
- Orchestration blast-radius controls (anti-affinity, restart pacing) are critical when changes can interact with customer network behavior.
